summary: PulseGuard v0.6.6 polishes Hardware Health into a clearer customer-facing diagnostic without changing the checks that v0.6.5 proved reliable.

sections.heading: Clear warning reason
sections.detail: The Hardware Health summary now explains why Overall is WARNING or FAIL. A warning caused only by crash history is labeled as historical crash / BSOD evidence rather than implying the current hardware failed.

sections.heading: Meaningful evidence labels
sections.detail: Generic Local Windows evidence labels are replaced with SMART / Windows storage reliability, Windows WHEA event log, BugCheck + minidump history, Device Manager / PnP status, Gateway + DNS + Internet, and Windows battery telemetry.

sections.heading: Plain-English details
sections.detail: Storage and other rows use plain-English customer wording, the Count column is now Findings with explicit 0 or N/A markers, and raw-looking disk status strings are no longer the primary explanation.

sections.heading: Historical crash context
sections.detail: Selecting Crash / BSOD History now shows recent bugcheck timestamps, codes, minidump evidence, and an explicit note that historical crash evidence is not proof of a current hardware failure.

sections.heading: Prominent result layout
sections.detail: The small Hardware Health summary was moved below the check table into a larger bold result block, with selected evidence directly underneath so PASS/WARNING/FAIL and its reason are immediately visible.
